challenge: Victoria Crater steep rim climb through a loose boulder field (Gen 0 edge: 0.35 m rocks)

challenge_spec.title: Victoria Crater steep rim climb through a loose boulder field (Gen 0 edge: 0.35 m rocks)
assumptions: Terrain: real elevation data, Victoria Crater (Opportunity), Mars (U01 uncontrolled) (80 m square, 5.3 m of relief, typical slope 9.5°). Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona HiRISE DTM.
Gravity set to 3.71 m/s² for mars.
Friction set to 0.7 for a regolith surface.
Loose regolith friction is set to 0.65 (calibration range 0.45–0.65); 12 path rocks are 0.20 m high (calibration range 0.15–0.35 m).
Must fit the lander: ≤ 12 kg, ≤ 0.8 × 0.5 m.
Escalated after a verified generation-zero design failed with approximately 0.35 m rocks.
